definitions.event: CPU above the threshold at the target row t+3 (90 s ahead); one per window
definitions.precision, recall, f1: window level: alarm = forecast above the threshold
definitions.false_alarms_per_day: alarm episodes (runs of consecutive alarm windows) that overlap no window whose target row is above the threshold, per day
definitions.lead time: evaluate.py: (onset - t) x 30 s for the earliest t in [onset-3, onset-1] whose forecast exceeds the threshold, else 0 (missed)
definitions.ceiling_lead_s: no input changes before a spike's first ramp row, so no forecast made earlier is informed: min(onset - ramp start, 3) x 30 s
definitions.crossings: changes of (forecast > threshold) between consecutive windows (evaluate.py's 'oscillations')
definitions.spurious/missed crossings: forecast and true crossings matched one-to-one when they have the same direction and are at most 3 windows apart; unmatched forecast crossings are spurious, unmatched true ones missed. A forecast crossing that comes more than 3 windows early or late counts once as spurious and once as missed
definitions.spike_*: lead time over spike onsets only: the first crossing of the threshold inside each generated spike that reaches it. evaluate.py's onsets (lead_mean_s) also include normal-load noise crossings below 75% and re-crossings during a spike's hold above 75%; at exactly 75% the two coincide
definitions.noise floor: error of an oracle that knows the generator's noiseless base load (seasonal_cpu) but not its N(0, 3^2) noise: normal rows, and post-scaling rows (0.8 x seasonal against recorded CPU)
definitions.coverage: share of windows with actual CPU at t+3 <= mean + k sigma (one-sided)
definitions.k_for_coverage: the empirical quantile of (actual - mean) / sigma: the multiplier that would have reached that coverage ON THE TEST SET (descriptive; a deployed k must be chosen on validation data)
definitions.diebold_mariano: d = loss(ProximaScale) - loss(baseline); Newey-West (Bartlett) long-run variance; negative statistic = ProximaScale better; two-sided normal p-value
definitions.block bootstrap: moving blocks of 120 windows, 2000 replicates, same blocks for every method (paired), percentile 95% CI
definitions.spike bootstrap: the spikes resampled with replacement, 10000 replicates
definitions.seed aggregation: mean and sd (ddof=1) over the dump's MC seeds; for CIs and p-values, the most conservative seed
